item.title: 14 provinces, one dream
item.description: Veiyasana Knight gives overlooked young league players a chance to chase their dreams For Veiyasana Knight under-17 coach Apisalome Nabose, missing out on selection for an established rugby league club should not mean the end of a young player’s dream.
item.content:encoded:
Veiyasana Knight gives overlooked young league players a chance to chase their dreams

For Veiyasana Knight under-17 coach Apisalome Nabose, missing out on selection for an established rugby league club should not mean the end of a young player’s dream.

The newly formed club is providing that second chance, defeating Topline Warriors 12-4 in round nine of the Eastern State Rugby League club competition.

Nabose and his father, who were among the founders of Davuilevu Knights, established the club to give aspiring players who could not make clubs such as Davuilevu Knights, Makoi Bulldogs and Nadera Panthers an opportunity to continue playing.

Nabose said the club’s name reflected its purpose.

“Veiyasana means for every province,” he said.

The aim is to cater for players from all 14 provinces of Fiji.

The response has been overwhelming, with players travelling from as far as Navutulevu in Serua, Nabukavesi in Namosi, Noco in Rewa, Lami and the interior of Tailevu for training and matches.

Without a proper training ground, the club trains every Tuesday and Thursday at Saint Joseph the Worker Primary School in Nakasi, with Nabose thanking the school for allowing the team to use its grounds.

Despite the long journeys, players continue to attend consistently and give their all at training.

“They come and train the house down,” Nabose said.

Their commitment has made selecting the 17-member match-day squad difficult.

With no financial sponsor this season, Nabose and his father also pay the players’ return fares for training and match days.

For Nabose, the sacrifice is worthwhile because rugby league can provide another pathway for young people seeking a future.

“Most of my players are not gifted inside the classrooms, so this opportunity is something big for them,” he said.

He hopes the players can eventually secure opportunities overseas and build careers through rugby league.

Nabose is now calling on companies and organisations to support the club next season as it seeks to give more young players an opportunity to make a name for themselves.

item.title: Malolo hold off Ba fight back in Lautoka
item.description: MALOLO Rugby held their nerve to secure a hard-fought 25-22 victory over Vinod Patel Ba Rugby Union at Churchill Park Ground Three yesterday. Malolo went into halftime with a commanding 15-0 lead after dominating the opening 40 minutes with strong attacking play and a solid defensive effort.
item.content:encoded:
MALOLO Rugby held their nerve to secure a hard-fought 25-22 victory over Vinod Patel Ba Rugby Union at Churchill Park Ground Three yesterday.

Malolo went into halftime with a commanding 15-0 lead after dominating the opening 40 minutes with strong attacking play and a solid defensive effort.

However, Ba returned from the break with renewed determination and mounted a strong fightback, putting Malolo under pressure in the second half.

The home side’s resurgence made for a tense finish, but Malolo managed to withstand the pressure and hold on for the three-point victory.

Malolo captain Imanueli Bari praised his teammates for their effort and credited Ba for providing a tough challenge.

“I thank the Ba team for giving us a good challenge and giving us a good game.

“It was a tough second half, and I thank the Malolo boys for a great effort. Now we will go back and regroup, ” Bari said.

Malolo will now turn their attention to their next assignment as they look to build on the hard-earned victory.

item.title: Fijiana sharpen basics
item.description: THE Vodafone Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says the side is using its preparation period to sharpen the basics as it builds towards a one-off Test against Japan on September 4. The Fijiana XV squad trained in Nadi yesterday as preparations continued for the important international fixture before the team heads to Hong Kong for the WXV Global Series Challenger from September 13 to 26.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says the side is using its preparation period to sharpen the basics as it builds towards a one-off Test against Japan on September 4.

The Fijiana XV squad trained in Nadi yesterday as preparations continued for the important international fixture before the team heads to Hong Kong for the WXV Global Series Challenger from September 13 to 26.

Walker said the team had spent the week learning, consolidating its work and addressing areas that needed improvement following its recent Test against South Africa.

“It’s been good. This week’s been full of learning and in the last couple of days we’ve tried to consolidate some of that learning,” Walker said.

He said the coaching staff had identified several areas they wanted to improve and had worked hard to bring those changes into the team’s current campaign.

Walker believes the squad possesses enough natural talent to create opportunities but stressed that the players must first execute the fundamentals.

“The ability that we’ll carry to play in space, to play with flair, it’s not something that I need to worry about. My focus is making sure that we do the basics really well,” he said.

That means making tackles consistently, retaining possession and showing patience when building attacking phases.

Walker said if the players could control those aspects of their game, opportunities to score would come naturally.

The Fijiana XV coach is also expecting a demanding challenge from Japan, describing them as a fast, structured and disciplined side.

He said Fiji would need to be sharp and clinical in possession while ensuring support players arrive quickly at breakdowns. He added Japan would be relentless throughout the 80 minutes. Walker believes controlling possession and gradually wearing Japan down will be crucial as Fijiana XV continues its preparations for the Test.

item.title: Kadavu power past Lautoka
item.description: KADAVU women overcame a difficult preparation in Kadavu to record a convincing 41-15 victory over Lautoka in the Subrails Marama Cup at Churchill Park yesterday. Coach Etuate Nauro said the team had faced several challenges in the lead-up to the match, particularly the wet weather and lack of suitable grounds to train on in Kadavu.
item.content:encoded:
KADAVU women overcame a difficult preparation in Kadavu to record a convincing 41-15 victory over Lautoka in the Subrails Marama Cup at Churchill Park yesterday.

Coach Etuate Nauro said the team had faced several challenges in the lead-up to the match, particularly the wet weather and lack of suitable grounds to train on in Kadavu.

“We came through after a lot of challenges and struggles back in Kadavu. The weather was rainy and we could not find a good ground to train on, also considering the travelling time to Lautoka,” Nauro said.

He said despite the difficulties, the players remained committed and their efforts were rewarded with a strong performance on the field.

“We thank the girls for all the effort they have shown us,” he said.

Kadavu dominated from the opening whistle, producing strong attacking and defensive plays to take a commanding 24-0 lead at halftime.

Meredani Qoro scored twice, while Sereima Rauqe and Salanieta Navatasi added a try each. Matelita Nunia converted two tries.

Kadavu continued their dominance after the break, maintaining possession and pressure to score three more tries through Vatiseva Cavuru, Nunia and Ulumila Likubai, with Livia Senibulileka adding a conversion.

Lautoka regrouped in the second half and showed more attacking intent, scoring three tries through Lotaini Loalala, Ruth Tinai and Camari Tora.

However, Kadavu held firm to secure the 41-15 victory.

item.title: Young Lionesses overcome MGM in U15 final
item.description: Suva Grammar School refused to blink when the pressure reached boiling point, holding off a late Mahatma Gandhi Memorial High School fightback to win a pulsating 20-18 under-15 final of the Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball Championships yesterday. It was a final decided by two points, but those two points came after a bruising battle in which neither side was willing to surrender the nati
item.content:encoded:
Suva Grammar School refused to blink when the pressure reached boiling point, holding off a late Mahatma Gandhi Memorial High School fightback to win a pulsating 20-18 under-15 final of the Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball Championships yesterday.

It was a final decided by two points, but those two points came after a bruising battle in which neither side was willing to surrender the national crown.

The lead changed hands repeatedly as SGS and MGM traded baskets in an intense opening to the national finals.

There was little to separate the two teams, with every possession carrying the weight of a championship and every mistake threatening to change the course of the match.

Then came the moment that ultimately decided the title.

An MGM error inside the final five minutes allowed SGS to stretch its advantage to 20-16.

Four points may have seemed insignificant in a match this tight, but it proved to be the opening the young Lionesses needed.

MGM fought back desperately, cutting the deficit to two, but SGS held firm as the clock ran down to protect its slender advantage and claim the national title.

For SGS team manager Georgina Batisaresare, the victory was a reward for a group of girls who had already endured disappointment the previous week.

Many of the players also compete in netball and were unable to complete their finals matches last week because of the weather.

Instead of breaking their spirit, the setback strengthened their resolve.

“After what happened last week, the girls came into the finals this week eager to compete,” Batisaresare said.

At halftime, the coaching staff knew the players needed more than tactics to overcome an opponent refusing to give ground.

The message was simple — enjoy the moment, but show how badly they wanted the championship.

“We simply told them, have fun but show them how much you really wanted the title,” she said.

“At the end of the match, the result will show who wanted it the most, and the girls did just that.”

When the final whistle sounded, the scoreboard showed only a two-point difference.

But for SGS, those two points represented composure under pressure, resilience after disappointment and the hunger to finish what they had started.

The young Lionesses had survived the national final — and emerged champions.

item.title: Church College of Fiji survive SVC thriller
item.description: Church College Fiji turned a remarkable school campaign into a national title after edging Swami Vivekananda College 31-29 in a high-drama Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball Championship under-15 boys final at the Vodafone Arena in Suva yesterday. The victory was special for CCF after all its teams reached the semi-finals, but the U15 boys were the only side to progress to the final — and t
item.content:encoded:
Church College Fiji turned a remarkable school campaign into a national title after edging Swami Vivekananda College 31-29 in a high-drama Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball Championship under-15 boys final at the Vodafone Arena in Suva yesterday.

The victory was special for CCF after all its teams reached the semi-finals, but the U15 boys were the only side to progress to the final — and they made the opportunity count.

CCF started strongly and controlled much of the first half before a lapse in concentration allowed SVC to claw their way back.

SVC dominated large periods of the second half, turning the contest into a tense battle that could have gone either way.

CCF captain Nathaniel Levaci said the coaches delivered a simple message at halftime.

“The message from the coaches was straightforward — ‘if not now, when?’ So we gave our hardest in the last 15 minutes,” Levaci said.

He said winning the title meant a lot to the team after their hard work throughout the season.

“It means so much to me and the team because all our hard work has finally paid off,” he said.

Head coach Marij Whippy said the team’s motto throughout the season was to play every match as though it was their last.

“In the last game the team stayed true to that motto,” Whippy said.

She praised SVC, saying the strong opponents pushed CCF to the limit.

“The match could have gone either way. In every sport, one team has to lose, but I have nothing but respect and admiration for our opponents,” Whippy said.

item.title: Ravuiwasa: It’s never too late
item.description: FOR Inoke Ravuiwasa, earning his first call-up to the Flying Fijians is more than a career milestone, it is proof that patience, sacrifice and belief can eventually open the door to a long-awaited opportunity. The rugby player is grateful for the chance to join the national squad and believes his selection is only the beginning of what he hopes will be a bigger journey.
item.content:encoded:
FOR Inoke Ravuiwasa, earning his first call-up to the Flying Fijians is more than a career milestone, it is proof that patience, sacrifice and belief can eventually open the door to a long-awaited opportunity.

The rugby player is grateful for the chance to join the national squad and believes his selection is only the beginning of what he hopes will be a bigger journey.

Ravuiwasa credited his family for standing behind him throughout his career, particularly through their prayers and constant support.

He also carries the memory of his late father, who was a rugby player, with him as he takes this next step in his career.

Being named in the Flying Fijians squad has also given Ravuiwasa the chance to reunite with former teammates from the Suva Rugby Union, making the opportunity even more special.

He said sharing the national environment with players he had previously played alongside was something he was thankful for.

But Ravuiwasa is not satisfied with simply making the Flying Fijians.

He has set his sights beyond the national team and sees his selection as the beginning of a much bigger journey.

“This is an opening door to many other greater doors,” he said.

For Ravuiwasa, the road to the Flying Fijians is also a reminder that sporting dreams do not have an expiry date.

His message to other aspiring players is simple: it is never too late to achieve a goal.

“It’s never too late. I’m living proof that it’s never too late to achieve your goal,” he said.

Ravuiwasa believes the right mindset and willingness to make sacrifices are crucial for anyone chasing a dream.

He knows the next stage will bring greater expectations and tougher challenges, but he is ready to embrace the opportunity.

item.title: Suva women maintain run
item.description: SUVA women continued their winning run in the Subrails Marama Cup Championship after a convincing 47-5 victory over Rewa in round 5 at the Suva Grammar School grounds yesterday. The win was Suva’s second consecutive victory and added to the side’s confidence as it prepares for the next round of the championship.
item.content:encoded:
SUVA women continued their winning run in the Subrails Marama Cup Championship after a convincing 47-5 victory over Rewa in round 5 at the Suva Grammar School grounds yesterday.

The win was Suva’s second consecutive victory and added to the side’s confidence as it prepares for the next round of the championship.

Captain Elenoa Matanisiga said the team was pleased with its performance but knew there were still areas that needed improvement.

“It was a good performance. I would also like to thank the team for the effort put into the field,” Matanisiga said.

Matanisiga said the team would use the week to work on the small areas identified from the match and its previous games.

She is taking up the captaincy for the third time and said leadership required individual preparation as well as teamwork.

“It all comes down to mentality and preparation individually for me. I would say it’s not easy leading the team, but it requires teamwork for the team to work well together,” she said.

Suva will now look to build on its back-to-back victories and maintain its momentum as the Subrails Marama Cup Championship progresses.
